action: Position the patient in the left lateral decubitus position.
interpretation: Prepare patient positioning to optimize the acoustic window.

action: Orient the probe in a sagittal (longitudinal) section. Ensure the pointer is directed towards the patient's head.
Scan and follow the margin of the liver.
interpretation: Use the liver margin as a guide to locate the gallbladder.

action: Adjust the view until the gallbladder appears.
interpretation: Visualize the 'exclamation mark' sign, identifying the gallbladder as the 'upper part' of the mark.

action: Identify the structure inferior to the gallbladder.
interpretation: Visualize the portal vein appearing as 'the dot' of the exclamation mark.

action: Once the gallbladder is in view, fan through the organ. Interrogate the entire gallbladder, paying particular attention to the neck.
interpretation: Perform a complete volumetric survey of the gallbladder anatomy.
Look for stones, characterized as 'white echogenic areas' that 'cast shadows'.

action: Assess the current view for pathology.
interpretation: Confirm that 'no stones' are visible in this sagittal view.

action: Rotate the probe to a transverse orientation. Interrogate the gallbladder in this orthogonal plane.
interpretation: Examine the gallbladder anatomy in a different plane to verify findings.
Re-confirm negative findings: 'don't see any stones' in this second plane.
